newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANALYSTS SEE MUCH LOWER WMC YEAR PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSTS SEE MUCH LOWER WMC YEAR PROFIT.

text.p: Weak base metal prices are expected to take the shine off WMC Ltd's results with analysts tipping a sharp fall in full year net profit to June 30.
Forecasts for WMC's net profit before abnormals, due on Wednesday, ranged from A$195 million to A$240 million.

The average estimate of A$217.5 million is about 44 percent lower than the group's 1995/96 net pre-abnormals figure of A$386.2 million but includes a second half that is eight percent higher than the 1996/97 first half outcome of A$104.4 million.
"The second half should see better throughput and volumes for most of the company's operations," said Prudential-Bache Securities analyst Tony Robson.

"Because there has been no big increase in metals prices the company was never going to get a big increase in its second half earnings," said Robson, who pegged his full year profit expectation at A$234 million.
In June, WMC managing director Hugh Morgan told an analysts meeting that he expected full year profit to be in line with their expectations.

Morgan's prediction followed a shutdown of the Kalgoorlie nickel smelter in Western Australia starting in April and lasting 42 days which he said would hurt the group's bottom line due to lost revenues.
Robson said at the time Morgan made these statements analysts forecasts were bunched mainly between A$225 million to A$235 million.
BZW Australia analyst John MacKinnon forecasts full year net profit before abnormals of A$210 million.
MacKinnon said this estimate reflected a flat second half for the group based on lacklustre gold, copper, nickel and uranium prices during the half.
